# [Set up]{.underline}

## [packages]{.underline}

```{r setup}
#The following code was not written by the group. Credit goes to Scott
# Download these packages. 
required_packages <-function(...) { 
  libs<-unlist(list(...)) 
  req<-suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(unlist(lapply(libs,require,character.only=TRUE)))) 
  need<-libs[req==FALSE] 
  if(length(need)>0){ 
    install.packages(need, repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org") 
    lapply(need, library, character.only=TRUE) 
  }
  else{message("No packages required installation.")} 
}

required_packages("tidyverse", "emmeans", "readxl", "lme4", "lmerTest", "auk", "terrainr", "ggrepel", "sf", "rebird", "kableExtra", "broom.mixed")

sites <- data.frame(
  Campus = c("SDSU", "CSUSM", "CSUSB", "CSULB", "Cal Poly", "UCLA", "Whittier","Scripps", "HMC", "CLU", "Pepperdine"),
  Latitude  = c(32.77466, 33.12919, 34.18227, 33.78210, 35.30927, 34.07142, 33.97764, 34.10376, 34.10604, 34.22781, 34.04022),
  Longitude = c(-117.07259, -117.15697, -117.31864, -118.11464, -120.66155, -118.44289, -118.02909, -117.71214, -117.70854, -118.87794, -118.70718)
)
#This  chunk of code is to put all of the different study sites into a data frame using their latitude and longitude. Download the required packages. Code in the begining is from Scott Apleby. 
```

## [Function creation]{.underline}

```{r temp-conversion}
f_to_c <- function(Far) {
  Cel <- ((Far-32)* (5/9))
  return(Cel)
}
#function made. Converting fahrenheit to celsius. Used in our data frame to convert when needed. 
```

## [Data upload]{.underline}

```{r Data}
HOBO_data_half_hour <- read_xlsx("Ambient_Data.xlsx") |> 
  select(!c(Season, Time, Month)) #read in from an excel file, selected relevant columns 
PRISM_data <- read.csv("PRISM.csv", skip = 10) |>  #read in csv file, assign column names. 
  dplyr::rename(Elevation = Elevation..ft.,
                Temp_avg = tmean..degrees.F.,
                Temp_max = tmax..degrees.F.,
                Temp_min = tmin..degrees.F., 
                Campus = Name) |> 
  mutate(Origin = "Climate",#apply function from F to C degrees. 
         Temp_avg = f_to_c(Temp_avg),
         Temp_min = f_to_c(Temp_min),
         Temp_max = f_to_c(Temp_max),
         Date = ymd(Date), #assign YMD formatting 
         Campus = str_replace(Campus, "Cal Poly SLO", "Cal Poly"), 
         Campus = str_replace(Campus, "Whitter", "Whittier"),
         Campus = str_replace(Campus, "Harvey Mudd", "HMC")) |> #make new columns with clean column names
  filter(Campus != "CSUSM")
```

## [Adjusting temporal scale]{.underline}

```{r Daily-Average}
HOBO_data <- HOBO_data_half_hour |> 
  group_by(MonthDayYear, Site, Campus) |> 
  summarize(Temp_avg = mean(Temperature),
            Temp_min = min(Temperature), 
            Temp_max = max(Temperature),
            .groups = "drop_last") |> 
  dplyr::rename(Date = MonthDayYear) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  as.data.frame() |> 
  mutate(Date = ymd(Date),
         Origin = "Microhabitat")
#make a new data frme with HOBO data, formatted with statical analyis of mean, min, and max temperature. 
HOBO_data <- HOBO_data |> 
  left_join(sites, 
            by = "Campus")
#combine hobo data info into main hobo data frame. 
```

## [Joining datasets]{.underline}

```{r join}
Temp_all <- HOBO_data |> 
  full_join(PRISM_data, 
            by = c("Date", "Campus", "Origin", "Temp_avg", "Temp_min", "Temp_max", "Latitude", "Longitude")) |> 
  mutate(Site = str_replace(Site, "Off", "Non-Urban"),
         Site = str_replace(Site, "On", "Urban"),
         Origin_sp = paste(Site, Origin, sep = " "),
         Origin_sp = str_replace(Origin_sp, "NA ", ""), 
         Month = as.factor(month(Date))) |> 
  filter(Month != 9 ) 
##Join prism data into hobo dataframe.
Temp_all_long <- Temp_all |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Temp_avg", "Temp_min", "Temp_max"), 
               names_to = "Metric", 
               values_to = "Temperature") |> 
  mutate(Metric = str_replace(Metric, "Temp_avg", "Average Temperature"),
         Metric = str_replace(Metric, "Temp_min", "Minimum Temperature"), 
         Metric = str_replace(Metric, "Temp_max", "Maximum Temperature"))
#Pivot the data into a single column to make a figure in the next step. 
```

## [Campus locations]{.underline}

```{r sages-attempt-at-mapping}

lizard_geo <- st_as_sf(sites,coords=c(x="Longitude",y="Latitude"),crs="WGS84") #Converts a regular dataframe → sf (simple features) object

lizard_geo_buf <- lizard_geo |> st_buffer(dist = 2000)

lizard_tiles <- get_tiles(lizard_geo_buf, services = "USGSTopo", resolution = 200) #Downloads map imagery (tiles) for your spatial extent

ggplot() +
  geom_spatial_rgb(data = lizard_tiles$USGSTopo, mapping = aes(x, y, r = red, g = green, b = blue)) +
  geom_sf(data = lizard_geo, alpha = .75) +
  labs(title = "Campus Locations with HOBOs and PRISM Climate Data", 
       caption="Locations of HOBO temperature loggers and requested PRISM climate data. Coordinates of campus locations with HOBOs deployed were entered into PRISM database to receive minimum, maximum, and average daily temperatures",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude") +
  geom_label_repel(data = sites, aes(label = Campus, x = Longitude, y = Latitude), size = 5, box.padding = .5) +
  #ylim(32.5, 35.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 5) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
```

# [Analysis]{.underline}

## [Temperature ANOVAs]{.underline}

```{r ANOVA and table}
#| message: False
lmer_avg <- lmer(Temp_avg ~ Origin_sp + (1|Campus) + (1|Origin_sp:Campus),
                 data = Temp_all, REML = F)
lmer_min <- lmer(Temp_min ~ Origin_sp + (1|Campus) + (1|Origin_sp:Campus),
                 data = Temp_all, REML = F)
lmer_max <- lmer(Temp_max ~ Origin_sp + (1|Campus) + (1|Origin_sp:Campus),
                 data = Temp_all, REML = F)

anova(lmer_avg)
anova(lmer_min)
anova(lmer_max)

pairs(emmeans(lmer_max,
              ~ Origin_sp))
#Linear mixed effects models 
```

## [Model-adjusted graphs]{.underline}

```{r}
#| message: False
#| warning: False

adjusted_avg <- as.data.frame(emmeans(lmer_avg, ~ Origin_sp)) |> 
  mutate(Origin_sp=fct_relevel(Origin_sp,"Urban Microhabitat", "Non-Urban Microhabitat", "Climate"))
adjusted_min <- as.data.frame(emmeans(lmer_min, ~ Origin_sp)) |> 
  mutate(Origin_sp=fct_relevel(Origin_sp,"Urban Microhabitat", "Non-Urban Microhabitat", "Climate")) 
adjusted_max <- as.data.frame(emmeans(lmer_max, ~ Origin_sp)) |> 
  mutate(Origin_sp=fct_relevel(Origin_sp,"Urban Microhabitat", "Non-Urban Microhabitat", "Climate"))
#model-adjusted values for average
ggplot()+
  geom_jitter(data=Temp_all, alpha=.25, show.legend = F, aes(x=Origin_sp, y=Temp_avg, color=Origin_sp)) +

            aes(x = Origin_sp, y = emmean, color = Origin_sp), show.legend = F) +
```

## [Tables]{.underline}

```{r}
#| message: False
#beginning of sage's code for table
#creating data frames from the anova models
avg_anova_df <- data.frame(anova(lmer_avg))
min_anova_df <- data.frame(anova(lmer_min))
max_anova_df <- data.frame(anova(lmer_max))

anova_results_df <- rbind(avg_anova_df, min_anova_df, max_anova_df)
# turn anova results into a data frame. 
#combine dataframes 
anova_results_df <- cbind(
  Term = rownames(anova_results_df),
  anova_results_df)
#create a new column called "term"
rownames(anova_results_df) <- NULL
#remove rownames so table has clean numbering 
#create a html table from combined ANOVA data frame 
anova_results_df |>
  kable("html", 
        digits = 3,
          col.names = c( #rename the column headers in the displayed table
      "Term",
      "Sum Sq",
      "Mean Sq",
      "Num DF",
      "Den DF",
      "F - value",
      "P - value"
    )) |>
  #add styling to the HTML table 
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = "striped",
    full_width = FALSE
  ) |>
  #add a group row label for the average temperature ANOVA results 
  pack_rows("Average temperature", 1, nrow(avg_anova_df)) |>
  #add a grouped row label for the minimum temperature ANOVA results
  pack_rows("Minimum temperature", nrow(avg_anova_df) + 1,
            nrow(avg_anova_df) + nrow(min_anova_df)) |>
  #add a grouped row label for the max temperature ANOVA results 
  pack_rows("Maximum temperature", nrow(avg_anova_df) + nrow(min_anova_df) + 1,
            nrow(anova_results_df))
   
post_hoc_max <- data.frame(pairs(emmeans(lmer_max, ~ Origin_sp)))

post_hoc_max |> 
  kable("html", 
        digits = 3) |>
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = "striped",
    full_width = FALSE
  )

```

## [Lizard data]{.underline}

```{r}
McGinnis_threshold <- 35.9 #establishing the threshold
McGinnis_Pref <- Temp_all |> 
  mutate(
    across(c(Temp_avg, Temp_max, Temp_min),
           ~ if_else(is.na(.), NA_character_, #ignore NAs
                     if_else(. < McGinnis_threshold, "under", "over")), #determine whether the value is over or under the threshold
           .names = "{.col}_Threshold"),
    across(c(Temp_avg_Threshold, Temp_max_Threshold, Temp_min_Threshold), ~as.factor(.x)), #apply this to all of the temperature columns
    Month = as.factor(month(Date))) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Temp_avg_Threshold, Temp_max_Threshold, Temp_min_Threshold),
    names_to = "AvgMinMax", #whether it is the min, max, or average metric
    values_to = "Threshold") #under or under
#calculate the proportion of days that the maximum temperature exceed the threshold for lizards
Aggregated_McGinnis_Max <- McGinnis_Pref |> 
  filter(!is.na(Threshold), 
         AvgMinMax == "Temp_max_Threshold")  |> 
  group_by(Campus, Origin_sp, Month, AvgMinMax) |> 
  summarise(
    n_under = sum(Threshold == "under"),
    n_over  = sum(Threshold == "over"),
    n_total = n(),
    n_proportion_exceed = n_over/n_total, 
    .groups = "drop")

```

## [Lizard model & table]{.underline}

```{r}
#lizard threshold anova
lizard_max <- lmer(n_proportion_exceed ~ Origin_sp*Month +
                   (1|Campus) + (1|Origin_sp:Campus) + (1|Month:Campus),
                   data = Aggregated_McGinnis_Max, REML = F, 
                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")) #optimizer to help it run
anova(lizard_max)
lizard_data <- pairs(emmeans(lizard_max, ~ Origin_sp|Month)) #grabbing the post hoc to reformat it into a nice presentable graph

kable(lizard_data, "html",
        digits = 3) |> 
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = "striped", #make it pretty
    full_width = FALSE
  )|> #the following groups the months
  pack_rows("March", 1, 3) |>
  pack_rows("April", 4, 6) |>
  pack_rows("May", 7, 9) |>
  pack_rows("June", 10, 12) |>
  pack_rows("July", 13, 15) |>
  pack_rows("August", 16, 18) 

```
